title: Stephen Curry, Warriors agree on 2-year extension – report
summary: Stephen Curry reportedly takes a deal $20 million below the max to give the Warriors more salary-cap flexibility next offseason

blocks.text: SHOOTING GREAT. Stephen Curry in action for the Golden State Warriors.
Stephen Curry reportedly takes a deal $20 million below the max to give the Warriors more salary-cap flexibility next offseason
The Golden State Warriors and Stephen Curry agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension, ESPN reported.
The deal, according to the report, includes a player option for the 2028-29 season.

ESPN also reported that Curry will receive $20 million less than what he could have maxed out at to give the Warriors more salary-cap space for next offseason. According to the report, Curry and the team had been working on several contract ideas once he became eligible for a two-year, $136.7 million max deal in August.
If Curry plays through the 2028-29 campaign, it would be his 20th season, all with the Warriors.

The 38-year-old was limited to 43 games last season, with much of the time missed because of a lingering knee injury. Nonetheless, Curry averaged 26.6 points, 4.4 made three-pointers, and 11.3 attempted 3-pointers per game — all above his career averages.

A 12-time All-Star drafted seventh overall out of Davidson in 2009, Curry has two scoring titles, two MVP awards, and a Finals MVP award to go with four NBA championships. However, the Warriors are coming off a 37-45 season, their worst in a non-shortened season since going 36-46 in 2010-11.
Earlier this week, Curry said he wanted “no drama” with the contract talks, particularly with camp opening on Tuesday, September 29.

“The idea of getting back to work is exciting,” Curry said Wednesday, September 23. “I feel like I’ve taken advantage of the offseason. I feel like there’s no hesitation about where I’m at physically going in. … But I’m excited about getting back to work.”
Curry has career averages of 24.8 points, 4.0 made three-pointers, and 9.4 attempted per game. The latter two marks are NBA records, as is his career .912 free throw percentage.
He also holds the NBA career marks for three-pointers made (4,248) and attempted (10,073). – Rappler.com
